notes: All listed named objects (D6-1, D6-2, D6-3, J0546, J0927, J1235, J1332, J1637) are prior D6/HVWD literature targets used here for model comparison, so they are recorded as follow_up rather than candidates_found (T:p1-b9; T:p1-b13; T:p1-b15; T:p5-b8; T:p9-b0; T:p10-b1). D6-1, D6-2, and D6-3 (T:p1-b15; I:p9-b0): the supplied 'D6 1-3' (also rendered 'D61-3') is expanded to the three individual D6 stars, supported by 'the first three stars' and the figure label 'D6(1-3)'. D6-2 (T:p1-b15; T:p4-b4): retained despite the paper's view that it most likely does not arise from this scenario, because follow_up applies regardless of the current origin conclusion. J0546 (T:p5-b8; T:p9-b0; I:p9-b0; T:p10-b1): omitted from the main HR/Kiel model comparison as outside the model range, but still plotted among the observed D6 stars and included in the ejection-velocity comparison. J0927 (T:p9-b0; I:p9-b0; I:p6-b1; T:p10-b1): studied through the observed-D6 figures and velocity comparison, though not named in the narrative. J1332 (T:p8-b2): its hypervelocity interpretation is explicitly conditional ('assuming that J1332 is a hypervelocity star').

D6-1: No individual numerical values meeting the requested quantity definitions are reported for D6-1. The paper discusses D6-1 alongside D6-3 in model-observation comparisons and provides qualitative statements about their similar radii and uncertain ages (T:p5-b10; T:p6-b2), while Figures 6–7 and 11 show D6-1/D6-3 positions without giving individual astrometric, distance, parallax, proper-motion, radial-velocity, galactocentric-radius, Galactic-rest-frame-speed, or bound/unbound probabilities. Velocity ranges shown for D6-1,3 in Figure 13 are model/sample ejection-velocity contexts, not an individual Galactic rest-frame speed.

D6-2: D6-2 is discussed in T:p1-b15 and T:p4-b4. The paper states that D6-2 has the lowest velocity among the observed stars and that it rotates with a period of 15.4 hours (Chandra et al. 2022), but it does not report a numerical value for any of the requested quantities (ra, dec, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability) for D6-2. Its observational values are otherwise referred to previous work or shown only graphically.

D6-3: The paper discusses D6-3 only as part of grouped D6(1-3)/D6-1,3 samples (e.g., T:p1-b9, T:p5-b10, T:p6-b2, I:p10-b1) and does not report individual RA, Dec, distance, parallax, proper motions, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for D6-3. Grouped velocity ranges/averages and non-eligible stellar parameters (radius, Teff, log g) were not treated as individual D6-3 values.

J1235: J1235 is discussed only as an observed comparison object (e.g., T:p1-b15, T:p8-b3, T:p9-b0, T:p10-b1). The paper does not report individual right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper-motion components, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for J1235. Fig. 13 and its caption mention a min/max range and an average for the combined group D6-1,3/J1235/J0927 rather than individual J1235 values, and these ejection-velocity quantities are not the requested Galactic rest-frame velocity (T:p10-b1; I:p10-b1). Therefore no requested quantity is assigned.

J1637: No eligible quantities are reported for J1637. The paper gives only a projected rotational velocity upper limit of 40 km/s (T:p4-b4) and plots its effective temperature, radius, surface gravity, and ejection velocity (e.g., T:p6-b2, T:p9-b0, T:p10-b1); these are not among the requested quantities. The ejection velocity shown for J1637 is not a Galactic-rest-frame total space velocity, and no numerical value for it is stated in the text.

J0546: J0546 is mentioned only in Section 5 (T:p5-b8) as the hottest star omitted from the model comparison and in the Fig. 13 caption (T:p10-b1), where cyan lines indicate comparison ejection velocities for J1637 and J0546. The paper does not report equatorial coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for J0546. The Fig. 13 cyan line represents an ejection velocity used for model comparison, not a heliocentric/barycentric line-of-sight radial velocity, so it is not assigned to radial_velocity.

J0927: J0927 appears only in the caption of Fig. 13 (T:p10-b1), where its ejection velocity is included in a grouped black region rather than reported individually. No individual right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported for J0927 in the supplied material.

J1332: J1332 is only mentioned as a D6 object for which the hydrogen-dominated model of Werner et al. (2024) is adopted (T:p5-b8) and is plotted in the HR diagram (I:p9-b0). The paper gives no numerical values for the target's position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probabilities, and explicitly refers to Bhat et al. (2025) for its radius, surface temperature, and surface gravity values (T:p5-b8). No quantities are retained.
